analysis:
The only changed file is docs/developer/test.md, and the changes are documentation. The "Last updated" date moves from 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-04 (line 3). CI wording at ~1243 now says the runtime tests run on "the provider's macOS CI runners (see CI runner routing)" instead of Blacksmith runners. The darkbloom-route paragraph (head lines ~1803-1811) now says the test pins each routed job's lanes, fallback, timeout and read-only permissions, and keeps release workflows on literal Blacksmith runners. The macOS jobs of ci.yml are no longer described as pinned to literal Blacksmith runners.

The diff changes no code or workflow, so no control is weakened by the PR itself. The documented move of ci.yml macOS jobs to routed runners falls under CI runner routing. That routing is covered by the test script scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, which checks read-only permissions, fork PR handling, exact label grants and untrusted or plain-HTTP planes. The release workflows (signing, publication; A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034) are still documented as pinned to literal Blacksmith runners, so signing and secrets are not exposed to routed runners per this text.

I did not see the workflow YAML or the route script. I therefore cannot verify that the docs match the actual ci.yml change, or that routed jobs lack secrets access. A later pass on the .github workflows should confirm the documented claims. The threat model does not appear to need updating from this documentation change. The other text in the supplied units (cluster tests, the prefix cache SSD tier, T-041) is unchanged context. No new attack surface is introduced by these lines.
